post_copy: Most Shopify SEO advice focuses on titles and keywords. I am testing a small scanner that checks whether product pages have concrete product facts, like material, barcode, brand, reviews, and availability.

I scanned a batch of Shopify products and the most common product data gaps were missing barcode, material, and review signals. Product descriptions alone are not enough if the structured fields are thin.
I built a free product data repair scanner for Shopify products. It checks up to 20 products and shows which fields may make the catalog harder to understand, compare, and maintain.
One practical product data repair: make product descriptions include material, use case, dimensions, variant context, and brand. Concrete product facts are more useful than generic marketing copy.
If a store has 100+ products, manually checking product data quality is slow. A scan-first workflow helps find the products where missing fields have the biggest score impact.
Question for Shopify owners: when you upload new products, what takes longer: writing descriptions, filling product fields, or checking variants and barcodes?
Week one learning from product data scans: missing structured product details are more common than bad titles. Barcode, material, size, color, and review data matter.
Quick Shopify product data checklist: brand, description, image, availability, SKU, barcode, material, color, size, MPN, reviews, price, and product URL.
Product data repair is not magic. It is mostly making each product complete enough for shoppers, search crawlers, and AI tools to understand what it is and who it is for.
I am looking for Shopify merchants with 50+ products to test a free product data scan. It gives a score and missing field breakdown; no signup for the first scan.
For dropshipping and POD stores, repeated supplier descriptions make products harder to differentiate. Adding concrete product facts can improve both human clarity and AI readability.
A useful product audit should answer three questions: what is missing, which products matter first, and what action will raise the score fastest.
If you run a Shopify store, what would make a product data report useful enough to install an app: better descriptions, missing field checklist, bulk save, or weekly monitoring?
I am wrapping up a 14-day test of AiReady. The goal was simple: see whether Shopify merchants care about product data repair enough to scan, install, or pay. Sharing the learnings soon.
